title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers to identify churn drivers and at-risk segments. The overall churn rate is 37.7%. Key findings indicate that monthly contracts and an identified at-risk segment are primary drivers of customer loss, while Premium plan customers generate significantly higher lifetime value.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates are highest among Basic plan customers at 38.9%, followed by Standard at 36.7% and Premium at 36.6%.
Churn rates vary by signup cohort, with the 2024 cohort experiencing the highest rate of 39.8%, followed by 2021 (38.0%), 2023 (37.1%), and 2022 (36.7%).
Monthly contracts exhibit a churn rate of 48.3%, which is a 121.1% increase compared to the 21.9% rate for annual contracts.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets and low satisfaction shows a critical churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0) with a standard deviation of 13.2 months. The average satisfaction score is 3.42, though 27 customers have missing scores.
Lifetime value is highest for Premium customers at $1,817, compared to $869 for Standard and $463 for Basic. Premium LTV is 292.0% higher than Basic.

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not track customer behavior over time.
Satisfaction scores are missing for 27 customers, potentially biasing the average satisfaction metric.
The dataset lacks causal variables for churn; reported associations do not imply causation.
conclusion: To reduce churn, focus on converting monthly contracts to annual plans and prioritize support for the identified at-risk segment. The significant LTV gap for Premium customers reinforces the value of retaining this high-value group.
